name: XPRS 1.13.0-beta.1
body:
## XPRS 1.13.0-beta.1

A beta for testing discovery and file sharing.

### Finding archivers
- A fresh install with no Bluetooth neighbour and no station on its network now finds archivers over Reticulum and adopts one, with nothing to configure. Search and the public groups ranking then fill from it.
- Fixed: an archiver's callsign was dropped when its Reticulum announce also carried its role, so no archiver was ever known by name over the internet.
- A station announces on a public Reticulum hub at most once an hour per destination. Announcing every 30 seconds got it muted by the hub, so nobody could find it.
- A station keeps its hub connections instead of dropping one that is quiet for 30 seconds (that rule is for phones on battery).
- An archiver that is not in earshot is asked for its directory and groups index.

### Files
- One fetch per file, asking every station known to hold it; a redirect to another holder is followed.
- A file of more than one piece is fetched in pieces from several holders, each piece verified. Holders state the exact size when they accept.
- Stations remember who holds a file and advertise the files they hold, with a piece list for large ones.
- Fixed: two people fetching the same file from one station (neither was told it had arrived); a transfer that finished but was never claimed on a device with a suffixed callsign; small files re-sent over radio being discarded.
- A tapped file of unknown size is no longer stuck on the small-file lane.
- Download progress reports the lane the bytes arrive on and how many holders are in use, read from local state.

### Linux
- No Bluetooth error printed at start.

### Known limits in this beta
- A fresh client can wait up to an hour to hear an archiver on a public hub (the hub forwards an announce only when it is sent).
- Fetching in pieces has been tested between two server stations; phone-to-phone over Bluetooth has not been retested in this beta.
